column1: # t/malformed/EXPECTED.tsv -- 2026-09-11 (ROADMAP 14.2 "Errors with a position").
# One row per file in this directory: the file, and the line, col and
# production surface.parse_file(file) must raise a SurfaceError naming.
# Six productions are SYNTAX.md's own EBNF names (Task, Type, SpecFun,
# Stmt, Expr, Op, Id -- that is seven, but Id is only reached by the
# lexer's "unexpected character", not by the parser proper). Two rows use
# a SYNTAX.md HEADING instead, because SYNTAX.md names no production for
# either rule: "Strings as sequences of code points (v1)" (a char/string
# literal is Atom sugar with no EBNF name of its own, so its lexer errors
# -- unterminated literal, bad escape, wrong code-point count -- are filed
# under the SYNTAX.md section that documents the literal forms) and "What
# the notation refuses" (surface.py's non-associative Cmp precedence level
# has no SYNTAX.md name either; the chained-comparison rule is documented
# in that section's table, so its error is filed there). Both are listed
# in surface.py's SurfaceError docstring and in LIT_PRODUCTION/
# NO_CHAIN_HEADING beside the raise sites that use them.
# Measured: python3 t/test_surface_errors.py, which parses every file
# below and checks file/line/col/production all four (line, col and
# production are the three the ROADMAP bar names; file is checked too
# since parse_file must report which file was bad).
